title: The Web Doesn't Sit Still: Adversarial Self-Evolving Attacks on Search Agents
claim: A multi-part system couples attacker-defender co-evolution with an evolutionary optimizer, a controlled sandbox and fine-grained metrics to expose vulnerabilities.
layout: 3 regions: top-left loop diagram, top-right zoomed module, bottom flow plus metrics
description: A dense, multi-panel framework figure with a pale blue-to-red background. Top left shows the bi-level loop. A defender team (blue) and an attacker team (red) are linked by dashed circular arrows labeled Outer Loop and Inner Loop. They connect a valid attack strategy pool, ImmuneUpdate, the agent system context, and an updated strategy pool P_t. A zoom wedge opens into an orange CREO panel. It contains the attack strategy definition (mechanism, generalization, portrait). It also contains population evolution, with Round 0 initialization, mutation and crossover through an LLM optimizer, and contrastive labeling with yes/no icons. The bottom green band shows a deterministic sandbox flow: a sandbox, a knowledge base, a dynamic interceptor with hot-injection, an agent, and behavioral traces. It ends in three metric rows (Acc, ASR, APR) with formulas.
caption: Overview of the adversarial self-evolution framework. Left: Bi-level optimization drives attacker-defender co-evolution. Top Right: CREO drives directional mutation and crossover recombination of the attack strategy population via contrastive evolution signals. Bottom: The controlled sandbox ensures noise-free trace capture, while fine-grained metrics (Acc, ASR, APR) quantify the agent's internal cognitive vulnerabilities.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise for empowering search agents to tackle complex information-seeking tasks. However, since acquiring external information necessitates web search, these agents are highly susceptible to various adversarial attacks (e.g., malicious information injection or stealthy context manipulation). Existing attack strategies inevitably rely on static and human-crafted templates, failing to emulate the dynamic and complex nature of real-world threats. In this paper, we propose an adversarial self-evolution framework that integrates bi-level optimization between the attacker's strategy evolution and the defender's adaptive mitigation, to expose the vulnerabilities of search agents. Specifically, we introduce the Contrastive Rollout Evolutionary Optimization (CREO) method to drive the directional evolution of the attack strategy population via contrastive evolutionary signals. To provide a stable environment for this continuous evolution, we further construct a controlled sandbox and design fine-grained metrics to quantify internal vulnerabilities. Extensive experiments across various multi-hop QA benchmarks and frontier LLMs demonstrate that the proposed framework yields attack efficacy superior to static baselines, underscoring the urgent need to develop more robust defense frameworks.
